_note: This is the game's DEFAULT style — used for room backgrounds and in-room character sprites (the actual walkable game). Cutscene-only portrait art (the prologue slides) intentionally bypasses this file and uses hand-written prompts instead. Changed 2026-08-19 twice in one day: first from a close-up cinematic-portrait camera (rooms looked like a photo backdrop with cutouts standing in front), then AGAIN after that fix only changed the camera angle and kept the same painterly/cinematic/vignette rendering style, which produced murky, architecturally-unreadable rooms — confirmed by the user ('that house art makes no sense') pointing at Stardew Valley as the actual target look. Stardew is clean, bright, and crisply readable, not moody/painterly — this version names it explicitly and strips every bit of cinematic-portrait language (vignette, rim-lighting, dramatic shadow) that had carried over.
camera: Top-down RPG interior room view, in the exact style of Stardew Valley's building interiors: a clean, gently-angled overhead perspective, orthogonal walls, a clearly readable rectangular floor plane. NEVER an eye-level photograph, NEVER a close-up character-portrait crop, NEVER a dramatic/cinematic angle.
style: Crisp, clean 16-bit pixel art in the exact visual style of Stardew Valley: small clean pixels (NOT large chunky painterly blocks), flat-to-soft cel shading, bright even lighting with only gentle directional shadow. Explicitly avoid: moody cinematic rim-lighting, vignettes, heavy atmospheric haze, painterly gradient shading, dramatic single-light-source shadow. Every wall, the floor boundary, and every piece of furniture must have a sharp, clearly readable edge so the room instantly reads as a coherent rectangular space you could walk around in — not an ambiguous or half-obscured shape. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: small, clean, slightly chibi-proportioned full-body top-down sprite (like a Stardew Valley villager), head-to-feet, simple flat-shaded coloring matching the same clean style, no dramatic lighting on the character either.
palette: Saturated, cheerful, warm indoor lighting (soft yellow/amber lamp glow is fine) — but EVEN and bright across the whole room, not a dark moody scene with pools of shadow. Characters use clear, distinct flat colors so they read instantly against the room.
background: For a ROOM: a complete, evenly-lit top-down interior appropriate to the space, empty of any characters, with an unmistakable open floor area filling most of the lower frame. For a CHARACTER SPRITE: isolated on a transparent background, no scene/ground/shadow drawn in.
constraints: No text, no logos, no watermark, no UI elements, no borders/frames baked into the image. A room must have clean orthogonal architecture (walls meet the floor at a clear, readable line) — reject anything where the walls or furniture look melted, warped, or spatially incoherent. A character sprite must be full body head-to-feet, standing, facing toward the viewer — never a close-up bust/portrait crop. CRITICAL for any character sprite (not a room background): isolated ONLY on a plain transparent background — absolutely no scene, room, walls, furniture, or floor drawn in, just the character alone (confirmed failure mode without this exact wording: the model draws a whole room around the character instead of isolating them). Any character wearing glasses must have clearly visible human eyes — pupils and eye whites — showing behind the lenses, never blank/hidden skin tone (confirmed failure mode: glasses rendered with no eyes underneath).
